item.title: Boerse Stuttgart Records September Turnover Of Around EUR 16 Billion - Increases In All Asset Classes Compared To The Same Month Of The Previous Year
item.content:encoded:
Boerse Stuttgart is the German exchange of Boerse Stuttgart Group. The European group also operates exchanges in Sweden and Switzerland.

Based on the order book statistics, Boerse Stuttgart generated turnover of around EUR 16,1 billion in September, around 68 percent more than in the same month of the previous year.

Structured securities made up the largest share of the turnover. The trading volume in this asset class was around EUR 9,1 billion – an increase of around 105 percent compared to the same month of the previous year. Leverage products generated turnover of around EUR 7,7 billion. Investment products contributed around EUR 1,4 billion to the total turnover.

According to the order book, trading in equities produced turnover of around EUR 3,1 billion, 78 percent more than in the same month of the previous year. German equities contributed around EUR 898 million towards this total. International equities generated turnover of around EUR 2,2 billion.

The monthly total for trading in debt instruments (bonds) was around EUR 1,6 billion in September, around 31 percent more than in the same month of the previous year. Around EUR 662 million turnover was attributable to corporate bonds.

Turnover shown in the order book from exchange-traded products (ETPs) was around EUR 2,2 billion, around 6 percent more than in the same month of the previous year.

item.title: The Payments Association Acquires TPA EU To Accelerate International Expansion - Acquisition Of European Sister Organisation Creates A 350+ Member Payments Community And Marks The First Major Step In The Payments Association’s International Growth Strategy
item.content:encoded:
The Payments Association (TPA), the trade association representing the payments industry, has acquired its European sister organisation, The Payments Association EU (TPA EU), bringing the two communities under one umbrella and creating a combined network of more than 350 member organisations.

The acquisition, which follows a unanimous vote by TPA EU members, marks the first major step in The Payments Association’s strategy to build an international footprint and extend the reach, capabilities and value of its membership proposition beyond the UK.

TPA EU will retain its strong European identity and presence. The organisation will continue to be based in Luxembourg and led by General Manager Thibault de Barsy, ensuring continuity for its members and maintaining its focus on the priorities and opportunities shaping the European payments market. Anders la Cour will also continue to play a role supporting the community of Members.

The combined organisation will accelerate the opportunities for payments businesses to connect, collaborate and build relationships across the UK and the European Union. The wider community will include major international brands such as Amazon, BNP Paribas and Bytedance alongside banks, fintechs, payment providers and other organisations from across the payments ecosystem.

Emma Banymandhub, CEO of The Payments Association, said: “Our ambition is to improve payments globally, not only in the UK, and this acquisition is the first tangible step towards the international footprint we have set out to build.

“By bringing TPA EU fully into The Payments Association, we are creating a community of more than 350 members while giving our European operation greater resources and capabilities to grow. Crucially, this is not about running Europe from the UK. Thibault and his team will continue to lead TPA EU from the European Union, with the needs of European members firmly at the heart of what they do.

“What we can now add is the best of what we have developed in the UK – from advocacy and policy engagement to member programmes, commercial opportunities and community building – and use those capabilities to deliver even greater value to existing and future members across Europe.”

The acquisition builds on the investment in The Payments Association by global events and communities business Nineteen Group in 2025, which provided backing for the Association’s long-term growth ambitions.

A central focus of the next phase will be to bring proven practices, programmes and expertise developed by TPA in the UK to the European market, while adapting them to the distinct regulatory, commercial and political environment in which the EU members operate.

TPA intends to strengthen the advocacy and policy support available to European members by drawing on its experience of convening the payments industry and engaging policymakers and regulators in the UK. This includes its work representing industry concerns during the development of the UK’s mandatory Authorised Push Payment fraud reimbursement regime.

Thibault de Barsy, General Manager of The Payments Association EU, said: “From our base in Luxembourg, we have built a vibrant community of more than 80 payments organisations with its own identity and a deep understanding of the European market. That local focus will remain.

“What changes is the breadth of resources and expertise we can draw upon. Becoming part of the wider Payments Association gives us access to proven programmes, greater operational capability and a much larger international network. That will help us strengthen what we already offer our members and accelerate the growth of our community across Europe.”

For members on both sides of the Channel, the acquisition will also create greater opportunities for cross-border collaboration, knowledge-sharing and commercial connections at a time when payments businesses are increasingly operating across multiple markets and regulatory regimes.

Anders la Cour, Chairman of The Payments Association EU, commented: “The unanimous support of our members demonstrates the strength of the opportunity they see in bringing the two organisations together. TPA EU retains its European leadership and focus but now has the scale and backing of a much larger organisation behind it.

“That combination gives us an opportunity to build an even stronger European community while creating closer connections between payments businesses operating across the UK, Europe and internationally.”

The acquisition represents the beginning of a broader international growth strategy for The Payments Association, with the organisation seeking to build a more connected global payments community and extend the model it has developed in the UK into additional markets over time.

This is also an important milestone following Nineteen Group’s investment in The Payments Association.

Allison Jackson, CEO of Nineteen Group, said: “Our investment in The Payments Association was based on a shared ambition to grow its community, strengthen the value it provides to members and build its international reach. This acquisition is a significant first step in delivering against that ambition.

“It brings together two established communities while creating the platform and resources for further growth. We are excited to support Emma, Thibault and their teams as they develop The Payments Association’s presence in Europe and, over time, internationally.”

item.title: SIX Exchanges Figures: September 2026
item.content:encoded:
SIX publishes the monthly key figures of SIX Swiss Exchange and BME Exchange on trading and listing activities in Switzerland and Spain.

  • Tables of Current Month
  • Translations and Glossary

Trading turnover on SIX markets rises by a third in September

In September 2026, combined trading turnover for SIX Swiss Exchange and BME Exchange rose by a third (33.8%) compared to August, reaching CHF 168.5 bn while the number of transactions rose by 17.6% to 8,190,386. 

Equities reported the strongest performance on SIX Swiss Exchange, rising 33.8% month-on-month (MOM) and 30.3% year-on-year (YOY). This contributed to an overall increase in trading turnover on the Swiss market to reach CHF 111.9 bn, constituting growth of 28.2% compared to the previous month.

BME Exchange recorded a similarly positive uptick in overall trading turnover, with EUR 59.9 bn traded, representing a 45.4% rise on August. The securitized derivatives and fixed income segments led this growth, with turnover almost doubling for derivatives (94.7%) and for bond trading (92.4%) over the previous month. 

The Spanish blue chip index IBEX 35 concluded September at 19,426.0 points, down 2.7% from August, with the index returning 12.2% for 2026 to date. A similar trend was seen for the Swiss blue chip index SMI, which declined 3.2% to 13,830.3 points, but remained up 4.2% since the start of the year. 

September also saw the launch of SIX Market Signal. The new data marketplace improves access to real-time exchange data from SIX Swiss Exchange, BME Exchange and Aquis Exchange for both institutional and retail traders.

Gregor Braun, Head Cash Market Sales, Exchanges, SIX, commented: “As markets have moved out of the quieter summer period, it’s positive to see cross-market turnover growth on both SIX Swiss Exchange and BME Exchange. The launch of SIX Market Signal underscores another key milestone in removing accessibility and affordability barriers to high-quality exchange data in Europe. In the long term, this will help increase trading both across SIX markets and European markets as a whole.”

item.title: Tokenovate Appoints William L’Heveder As Chief Revenue Officer To Accelerate Growth - Former BMLL Executive Joins To Build On Tokenovate’s Market Momentum, Scale Commercial Growth And Drive Institutional Adoption
item.content:encoded:
Tokenovate, the UK financial technology company providing post-trade workflows-as-a-service and programmable settlement solutions, has appointed William L’Heveder as Chief Revenue Officer. 
 
L’Heveder brings more than a decade of experience acrosscapital markets, strategy and commercial leadership. He spent over seven years at BMLL, a provider of historical market data and analytics to global capital markets, where he helped scale the business and drive its commercial growth through to its acquisition in 2025, following earlier experience at Boston Consulting Group and as a derivatives trader.
 
His appointment comes as Tokenovate continues to build traction around Novat, its programmable settlement protocol for tokenised assets. Designed to address long-standing settlement inefficiencies through programmability and standardisation, Novat combines digital legal agreements, the FINOS Common Domain Model (CDM) and programmable settlement to automate complex post-trade processes, streamline operations and improve liquidity efficiency acrossglobal capital markets. 
In September, Tokenovate announced the first CDM-native intra-day repo settlement on the Canton Network using USDC issued by Circle, demonstrating the application of its technology to institutional digital markets. Also in September, Tokenovate demonstrated atomic settlement for intra-day repo transactions in the Bank of England’s Synchronisation Lab. 
As Chief Revenue Officer, L’Heveder will focus on building on this momentum by expanding Tokenovate’s commercial pipeline, developing new client opportunities, strengthening strategic relationships and helping convert growing market interest into long-term commercial partnerships.
Richard Baker, CEO and Founder of Tokenovate, commented: “We are delighted to welcome William to Tokenovate at such an important point in our growth. We have built strong foundations across our technology, partnerships and market proposition, and William brings exactly the experience we need as we scale the business.
 
“He has a strong track record of helping grow a capital markets technology company, building senior industry relationships and converting market opportunity into commercial success. I’m really excited to have him on the team as we broaden adoption of our platform, deepen engagement with the market and reach new clients.”
 
William L’Heveder, Chief Revenue Officer at Tokenovate, added: “Tokenovate has built strong momentum and is becoming a key player in shaping the future of wholesale digital markets, both in the UK and globally.
 
“I’m excited and grateful for the opportunity to join the team. Having experienced first-hand what it takes to scale a capital markets technology business, I’m looking forward to bringing that experience to Tokenovate, strengthening existing relationships, opening new opportunities and winning new clients as we drive broader institutional adoption of our post-trade workflows and programmable settlement solutions, including Novat.”

item.title: Teciem Accelerates Growth With Appointments Of Chief Technology Officer And Chief Customer Officer - New Executive Appointments Further Advance Teciem Commitment To Customer-Centric Innovation, Cloud Transformation And Delivering AI-Enabled Solutions Across Treasury And Capital Markets
item.content:encoded:
Teciem, a global provider of front-to-back treasury and capital markets software solutions, today announced two key additions to its executive leadership team, appointing Stefano Maestri as Chief Technology Officer and Strath Lanyon as Chief Customer Officer. Both executives will be based in London and report directly to Teciem CEO Wissam Khoury.

The appointments represent another milestone in delivering the long-term strategy of Teciem, expanding the leadership team and reinforcing commitment to innovation, customer success and sustained investment in products, people and clients.

Demand for modern treasury and capital markets technology continues to grow as financial institutions seek faster deployment, greater operational efficiency and access to continuous innovation. Teciem is helping customers respond to these challenges through cloud-native solutions that simplify operations while supporting future growth.

Stefano's appointment strengthens the ability of Teciem to accelerate product innovation, cloud transformation and technology investment, while Strath's appointment enhances the company's focus on customer outcomes, adoption and long-term success.

The complementary expertise they bring will help Teciem continue delivering trusted, front-to-back treasury and capital markets solutions, deepening customer partnerships and supporting financial institutions through increasingly complex transformation programs.

Wissam Khoury, Chief Executive Officer and Board Director, Teciem, commented:

"Following the launch of Teciem just over six months ago, we are continuing to grow our leadership team and reshape the future of treasury and capital markets technology. Stefano and Strath bring exceptional experience in technology innovation, cloud transformation, customer success and operational excellence. Their appointments reflect our commitment to helping clients modernize faster, realize greater value from their technology investments, and benefit from the next generation of AI-enabled solutions. We are delighted to welcome them both to Teciem as we continue our strategic transformation and strengthen our position as the partner of choice for financial institutions worldwide."

As Chief Technology Officer, Stefano Maestri will lead global engineering and platform strategy at Teciem, helping shape the next generation of treasury and capital markets technology. He will focus on accelerating product innovation, advancing cloud and AI capabilities, and ensuring the resilience, security and scalability of all Teciem solutions. A proven technology leader with a strong track record across financial services and software businesses, Stefano brings deep expertise in mission-critical systems, platform transformation and global engineering leadership.

As Chief Customer Officer, Strath Lanyon will lead customer success at Teciem, deepening client partnerships, accelerating adoption, driving co-innovation and strengthening the team's ability to help customers modernize, realize value faster and achieve their strategic objectives. He brings more than 20 years of experience building and scaling IP- and services-led businesses across capital markets, RegTech and data automation.

item.title: Swiss Cloud Pioneer Infomaniak Joins SIX Swiss Exchange
item.content:encoded:
Today, Infomaniak SA (Ticker "INFO"), a Swiss sovereign cloud and digital collaboration provider, started trading on SIX Swiss Exchange. Based on an opening price of CHF 56.00 per share, the market capitalization of the listed B-Shares stood at approximately CHF 262 million. The listing marks a significant milestone in Infomaniak's more than thirty-year growth journey and provides access to the public capital markets to support the company's next phase of development.


Marc Oehler (CEO, Infomaniak), Boris Siegenthaler (Chief Strategy Officer, Infomaniak) (from left)

Infomaniak listed on SIX Swiss Exchange via a reverse takeover of Perrot Duval Holding SA, becoming the first certified B Corp and the first sovereign cloud pure player listed on SIX Swiss Exchange. Following the completion of the transaction, the issued share capital of Infomaniak comprises 8,050,226 unlisted registered A-Shares, with a nominal value of CHF 0.025 each and 4,670,103 listed B-Shares, with a nominal value of CHF 0.25 each.

Infomaniak will be included in the in the Swiss Performance Index (SPI) family.

Founded in Geneva in 1994, Infomaniak has established itself as an independent cloud and digital infrastructure provider, offering sovereign cloud infrastructure, collaboration tools, AI services, data storage, web hosting and streaming solutions. The listing gives Infomaniak access to the capital markets, which could, where appropriate, support the continued expansion of its sovereign cloud infrastructure, including additional data center capacity in Switzerland, the enhancement of its cloud and collaboration services with deeper integration of AI, and its commercial expansion across Europe. At the same time, the company remains committed to its independence, Swiss roots, and sustainability. The Infomaniak Foundation will continue to hold the majority of the voting power through unlisted A-Shares. This structure ensures that strategic control remains aligned with the company's mission and values.

Marc Oehler, CEO, Infomaniak, says: “Today opens a new chapter for Infomaniak. Companies and organisations in Switzerland and across Europe are looking for sovereign alternatives in the cloud and in AI, and we have been building one in Switzerland for more than 30 years. Access to the capital markets would allow us to accelerate: more data center capacity, more research and development, more talent, and a stronger presence in Europe. We approach this listing with a long-term perspective and look forward to welcoming shareholders who share this vision and ambition.”

Tomas Kindler, Global Head Exchanges, SIX, says: “Infomaniak’s listing is an important milestone for Switzerland as a technology and innovation hub. The company demonstrates how innovative Swiss technology companies can grow, scale and access the Swiss public markets. It also highlights the role of SIX Swiss Exchange in connecting pioneering companies with investors and supporting long-term value creation. I am particularly pleased that, as a SIX IPO Academy alumnus, Infomaniak’s journey to the public markets has now culminated in a successful listing.”

Further information about Infomaniak: www.infomaniak.com.

item.title: Ping An Asset Management (Hong Kong) Launches Healthcare And AI ETFs Tracking Solactive Indices
item.content:encoded:
Solactive is pleased to further strengthen its collaboration with Ping An of China Asset Management (Hong Kong) Company Limited (“Ping An Asset Management

(Hong Kong)”) with the launch of two new ETFs. The Ping An Healthcare 50 Select ETF tracks the Solactive G2 Healthcare 50 Select Index, while the Ping An AI Select ETF tracks the Solactive G2 Artificial Intelligence Select Index.

Healthcare markets continue to evolve alongside advances in medical technology, changing demographic needs, and developments in the delivery of care. Across Hong Kong, China, and the United States, healthcare companies operate across areas ranging from pharmaceuticals and biotechnology to medical technology and healthcare services, reflecting the breadth and continued evolution of the sector.

The Solactive G2 Healthcare 50 Select Index captures leading healthcare companies listed in Hong Kong and the United States. Its eligible universe is subject to minimum size and liquidity requirements and focuses on securities classified within the healthcare sector. The final composition comprises up to 30 Hong Kong-listed and up to 20 U.S.-listed companies, selected by free-float market capitalization. Hong Kong-listed securities must additionally be eligible for Southbound Trading through the Shanghai-Hong Kong or Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect programs. Constituents are weighted by free-float market capitalization, with 62% allocated to Hong Kong-listed securities and 38% to U.S.-listed securities. Individual Hong Kong-listed constituents are capped at 8% and U.S.-listed constituents at 5%, while the five largest components may together account for no more than 55% of the index. The index is rebalanced quarterly.

Artificial intelligence is undergoing rapid development as its use expands across computing infrastructure, software platforms, and a growing range of applications. Continued developments in areas such as semiconductors, data infrastructure, AI platforms, and application software are contributing to the evolution of the AI ecosystem across the United States and Asia.

The Solactive G2 Artificial Intelligence Select Index provides exposure to companies associated with the artificial intelligence sector across the Hong Kong and U.S. equity markets. Companies are identified across three AI exposure buckets: AI Infrastructure, AI Platforms, and AI Applications. Following the application of liquidity requirements, eligible securities are ranked by free-float market capitalization, resulting in the selection of up to 20 Hong Kong-listed companies and up to 40 U.S.-listed companies. The index assigns 62% of its weight to eligible Hong Kong-listed constituents and 38% to U.S.-listed constituents, with each individual security capped at 10%. The index is rebalanced quarterly.

The ETFs were listed on 30 September 2026 on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under the following information,

ETFTICKER
Ping An Healthcare 50 Select ETF 03500.HK (HKD), 41500.HK (USD)
Ping An AI Select ETF 03510.HK (HKD), 41510.HK (USD)

 

Timo Pfeiffer, Chief Markets Officer at Solactive, commented: “We are pleased to deepen our collaboration with Ping An Asset Management (Hong Kong) with the launch of these two ETFs. Both healthcare and artificial intelligence continue to evolve rapidly, underscoring the importance of transparent and rules-based index solutions that reflect developments within these markets. We are delighted to support Ping An Asset Management (Hong Kong) with indices tailored to these distinct investment themes.”

Mr. Albert Wang, Head of Capital Markets and CIO of PAAMC HK, said: “As technological breakthroughs drive growth across the AI value chain, the Ping An AI Select ETF spans AI infrastructure, platforms and applications, diversifying exposure across technological pathways while capturing innovation-led opportunities. The Ping An Healthcare 50 Select ETF focuses on Chinese pharmaceutical companies spearheading global expansion and U.S. leaders in innovative medicines, offering one-stop access to the sector’s long-term global growth potential. We are delighted to launch these two ETFs with the support of Solactive, broadening investment choices for investors seeking to capture compelling growth opportunities in the global AI and healthcare sectors.”

item.title: Saudi Exchange Announces Enhancement To Market Order Behavior
item.content:encoded:
The Saudi Exchange announced an enhancement to Market Order behavior in the Main Market and Nomu – Parallel Market, as part of its continued efforts to develop the Saudi Capital Market. Effective Sunday, 4 October 2026, the updated mechanism will allow Market Orders to execute against available liquidity across multiple price levels within a maximum range of five ticks.

Following the change, a Market Order may continue executing against available liquidity across multiple price levels, within a maximum range of five ticks from the best price. Once the five-tick boundary is reached, or where no further liquidity is available within the range, any remaining unexecuted quantity will be converted into a Limit Order at the last executed price.

Accordingly, a Market Order may be executed across multiple price levels, depending on the quantities available in the order book and within the specified range.

The enhancement aims to improve the execution of Market Orders by providing broader access to available liquidity across eligible price levels, allowing a greater quantity of a Market Order to be executed immediately.

The enhancement aims to increase the quantity of a Market Order that may be executed immediately by allowing it to access additional available liquidity within the defined five-tick range. As a result, a Market Order may be executed across multiple price levels rather than at a single price level.

Mr.Mohammed Al Rumaih, CEO of the Saudi Exchange, said: “As part of our ongoing efforts to advance the Saudi Capital Market, the enhancement of the order execution mechanism in the Cash Market marks an important step in improving efficiency and supporting the evolving needs of investors and market participants. It also reflects our commitment to fostering a more transparent, reliable, and competitive market, while ensuring its readiness for future growth and development.”

The Market Order enhancement comes as part of the recent developments in the Saudi capital market, including structural enhancements to the derivatives market. It reflects Saudi Exchange’s continued commitment to advancing market efficiency, supporting liquidity, and broadening participation.

For more information on the updated Market Order behavior, please refer to the Factsheet [link].

item.title: UK Public M&A Q3 2026 Market Update – White & Case
item.content:encoded:
Key points:

  • Deal values soar: £39.3 billion aggregate deal value (YTD 2026: £75 billion; FY 2025: £38.2 billion)
  • Overseas bidders dominate - involved in deals accounting for 72% of deal volume and 94% of aggregate deal value YTD 2026. Overseas bidders involved in all but one of the £1bn+ deals announced this year
  • Active market: 21 firm offers (YTD 2026: 47; FY 2025: 56)
  • Eight £1 billion+ transactions (YTD 2026: 13; FY 2025: 12)
  • Listed bidders and PE both active: ten PE bidders (£19.3 billion); ten listed bidders (£19.4 billion); one unlisted strategic (£583 million)
  • More hostile offers and bear hugs: two hostile offers and four bear hug announcements (YTD 2026: four hostile offers; 14 bear hugs)
  • US bidders active: Involved in ten firm offers; £32.2 billion aggregate deal value (YTD 2026: 17 firm offers; £47.3 billion)
  • Hot sectors: 14 firm offers in Q3 2026 in industrials, oil & gas, real estate and technology sectors. High deal values in industrials (£14.5 billion) and real estate (£15 billion). Oil & gas (£776 million) and technology (£1.1 billion) activity concentrated at the lower end of the market
YTD 2026 trends:
  • Sectors: The top three sectors by deal value are:
    • Industrials: nine firm offers; £25.5 billion
    • Financial services: eight firm offers; £19.8 billion
    • Real estate: five firm offers; £15.2 billion
  • Global revenues: c. 60% of bids by overseas bidders were for a company that derived most of its revenue from overseas
     
  • Overseas bidder profile: In the US, it has mainly been PE bidders, but in Continental Europe it has mainly been strategics
  • US v Continental Europe: US: 17 firm offers; £47.3 billion v. Continental Europe: 11 firm offers; £22.6 billion

Commenting, Patrick Sarch, Head of UK Public M&A at global law firm White & Case LLP, said:

“Deal values are soaring as overseas bidders drive activity at the top of the market. With scale increasingly being rewarded with a valuation premium across UK, European and US markets, overseas acquirers are pursuing larger, platform-building UK transactions rather than smaller bolt-on deals.

“Foreign bidders are also being driven by the prolonged valuation gap between UK-listed companies and their international peers. As long as this persists, they will continue to target the UK’s world-class listed companies with global revenue profiles, strong cash generation and established management teams.

“Despite heightened geopolitical tensions, bidders are pressing ahead as they view waiting for calmer conditions as a risk. While concerns remain over what continued foreign takeovers mean for the future of the UK public markets, without more new companies being listed and scaling up, we welcome this inbound capital flow into our open economy from buyers who see opportunities to unlock greater value under private ownership. An absence of international demand would be far worse and there are encouraging signs of optimism for UK listed companies.”

Sonica Tolani, Partner in the global M&A and Corporate practice at global law firm White & Case LLP, added:

“Listed bidders remain active alongside private equity, showing that strategic buyers are prepared to compete for high-quality UK assets where there is a strong rationale for a transaction.

“We are also seeing more hostile offers and the growing use of bear hugs, with overseas bidders increasingly willing to make their proposed terms public and invite shareholders to put pressure on boards to engage. This reflects deeper familiarity with the UK regulatory environment, and a willingness to use public pressure as a legitimate tool rather than a last resort.

“Structural changes in the UK market are also making these tactics more effective. The UK market has lost domestic, long-term investors who would once have rallied behind target boards. That changing investor base is more vocal and, with many UK-listed companies continuing to trade at a sustained discount to international peers, shareholders may prefer a premium in hand over a board’s multi-year case for a higher standalone valuation.”
